note: Adversarial review findings (item-quality and compliance lenses) from the 15-17 Oct review round, recovered from the workflow transcripts after the device move. Not yet acted on.

item-quality.verdict: The task holds up apart from one real oracle defect. As a build/L1 composed-chain item it is correct, the instruction is self-contained and the gates are sound. The numbers are consistent (0.15·10^(16/20) = 0.946436, RMS 0.669231), the observation point and item type are named, the dev split matches signature_split, and level and family match the proposal definitions. Seven extra alternatives I wrote pass V5: Complex To Float, a Vector Source holding one 63-sample period, the old Throttle with a parallel Audio Sink, DC blockers, and a 4 kHz low-pass. The one fault (F1): the oracle has no transient skip, so correct answers that add a FIR filter, which the 'no harmonics' wording invites, are rejected depending on the filter design. I confirmed this with real ladder runs: a 5 kHz/1 kHz Hamming low-pass gives max_abs 0.997 against a 0.9938 limit, and a 2.6-3.0 kHz band-pass gives max_abs 1.017. An offline firdes scan rejects 50 of 138 filter designs that are correct once the filter has filled. Adding skip 4096 to every check, with n_items and min_items set to 12288, fixes this: every variant and filtered alternative then passes and all 12 mutants are still killed. The other findings are low-severity wording and coverage issues. The phrase 'with a gain stage' conflicts with registering v1, which has no gain block, as correct. The instruction gives away the dB-to-linear result. 'Do not limit the number of samples' is never checked. The variants' Throttle and const-source chains hash to the train split. The item should not be accepted until F1 is fixed. Scratch files: C:\Users\Lenovo\AppData\Local\Temp\claude\C--Users-Lenovo-Documents--MScAC-2701-ml-ops-project-project\e3a3c780-e6be-4b4a-8abe-931944b53353\scratchpad\rev01\ (scan_filters.py, fixcheck.py, run_alts.py, *.grc), with copies of the .grc files and run_alts.py in ~/grc-bench-work/review/gbf-dev-01/.

findings.claim: The oracle rejects correct answers that put a FIR filter in the chain. No check uses `skip`, so all five features are measured from sample 0, and a filter's start-up transient (overshoot or ramp-up) fails max_abs or rms even when the steady-state output meets every stated requirement. The instruction stresses "a single clean 2.8 kHz tone with no harmonics, noise or other tones", which makes adding a clean-up low-pass or band-pass filter a likely model choice. Whether such an answer passes then depends on the filter design.
findings.evidence:
Real ./gb ladder runs (scratch files in ~/grc-bench-work/review/gbf-dev-01/):
- c_lpf5k_1k.grc (the reference chain with low_pass_filter fir_filter_fff, cutoff 5000, width 1000, Hamming, after the gain; its gain at 2.8 kHz is 1.0022) fails V5: max_abs 0.997258 > 0.993758 (= 0.946436 × 1.05). It passes peak_freq, rms 0.6685, mean and band_fraction 0.995.
- c_lpf5k_before_gain.grc (the same filter placed before the gain): max_abs 0.997258, fails.
- c_bpf_2600_3000_100.grc: max_abs 1.0169, fails.
- c_bpf_2500_3100_200.grc: max_abs 1.0136, fails.
- b_bpf_2780_2820_50.grc: rms 0.6158 (-8 %), fails, while its steady-state max_abs is 0.946433.
- a_lpf.grc (cutoff 4000, width 1000) passes with max_abs 0.981, so the result depends on which filter the model picked.
Offline scan (rev01/scan_filters.py): GNU Radio firdes taps, oracles.evaluate on the first 8192 samples, which matches the ladder's 0.997258. Of 138 LPF/BPF designs (Hamming/Hann/Blackman) with 2.8 kHz in the passband, all 138 pass every check once the filter has filled, but 50 fail on the first 8192 samples. The cause is the cosine source starting at its peak, which acts like a step and makes the filter overshoot by about 5-9 %, plus the RMS deficit of long filters. The task brief says to "use skip to drop filter transients", and sibling items gbf-dev-02, gbf-dev-04, gbf-test-01 and gbf-test-11 use skip 4096.
findings.suggested_fix: Add "skip": 4096 to every oracle check and set observation.run n_items and min_items to 12288. I verified this with rev01/fixcheck.py: the reference, all 4 variants and the 5 filtered alternatives above all reach V5, and all 12 mutants are still killed (first_failed V5). Optionally also add a filtered variant (e.g. the low_pass_filter 5000/1000 chain) to variants/ so the gate guards this case.

findings.claim: The instruction asks for "a test-tone generator with a gain stage", which reads as a structural requirement, yet the author registers variants/v1_amp_on_source.grc (no gain stage; 0.15·10^(16/20) folded into the source amplitude) as a correct solution. Either the gain stage is required, in which case v1 is not a correct variant, or it is not, in which case the instruction states a requirement that is never graded. Reviewers reading the instruction and the variants will disagree.
findings.evidence: task.json instruction: "works as a test-tone generator with a gain stage ... amplify it by 16 dB". gates.json lists v1_amp_on_source.grc at ["V5", null]. The reference graph has a separate multiply_const block named 'gain', and v1 has no gain block at all.
findings.suggested_fix: Reword to a purely behavioural spec, e.g. "Build a GNU Radio flowgraph that generates a test tone ... and applies 16 dB of amplitude gain to it", or drop v1 and keep the structural wording, accepting that V5 cannot enforce it.

findings.claim: The instruction gives the computed result of the dB conversion ("peak amplitude of about 0.946 (an RMS level of about 0.669)"). That conversion is the only domain-reasoning step in this L1 build task, so stating its answer gives it away. A model can just set amp 0.946 without knowing what 16 dB means. As a result the two 'classic dB mistake' mutants (16 used as a linear factor; 16 dB read as a power ratio) test errors the instruction already rules out.
findings.evidence: task.json instruction: "The 16 dB is an amplitude (voltage) gain, so the amplified tone has a peak amplitude of about 0.946 (an RMS level of about 0.669), within 5 %". The phrase "amplitude (voltage) gain" alone already removes the ambiguity. build.py's docstring says the amplitude was stated "so the dB convention is unambiguous", but that goal is met without the number.
findings.suggested_fix: For the team to decide: keep "16 dB of amplitude (voltage) gain" and state the tolerance relative to it ("the output peak amplitude must be within 5 % of what this gain implies"), without the precomputed 0.946 and 0.669. The oracle values stay the same.

findings.claim: "The flowgraph should keep running until it is stopped; do not limit the number of samples" is a stated requirement that nothing checks. An answer that limits the output with a Head block of at least 8192 items passes.
findings.evidence: a_head.grc (the reference chain with blocks_head num_items 100000 before the File Sink) reaches V5 with every check passing. The ladder's 'finished_on_its_own' flag never affects the verdict (the reference itself reports finished_on_its_own=True). spec_properties only records "at least 8192 items delivered".
findings.suggested_fix: Present the sentence as a run condition the harness needs (or drop 'do not limit'), or record in spec_properties that only >= 8192 delivered items is checked, so reviewers do not expect enforcement.

findings.claim: The split rule protects only the reference's exact block sequence. Trivially equivalent chains used by this item's own variants hash to the train split, so a training-side L1 generator that follows the documented rule (signature_split(sig) == "train") could legally produce this same tone-gain-file task with a no-op Throttle inserted. The disjointness line covers only the existing training specs, not this route.
findings.evidence: compose.signature_split of the reference ('analog_sig_source_x','blocks_multiply_const_vxx','blocks_file_sink') gives dev, as required. But v2's ('analog_sig_source_x','blocks_throttle2','blocks_multiply_const_vxx','blocks_file_sink') gives train, and v4's ('analog_const_source_x','blocks_multiply_xx','blocks_file_sink') also gives train. v3's chain gives test. Sig source, Throttle, block, sink is the standard GRC idiom. Contamination here would inflate the dev scores used for checkpoint selection.
findings.suggested_fix: Before training-side chain generation starts, either normalise signatures (e.g. drop blocks_throttle/blocks_throttle2 before hashing; this item's split stays dev) or list this cluster's near-twin signatures as excluded from training. Optionally add a sentence on this to the item's disjointness field.

compliance.verdict: Mostly holds up: gbf-dev-01 is a correct, fair and essentially unambiguous dev item, with three low-severity wording/oracle-consistency issues (F1-F3). I re-ran ./gb tier-f gates on items/tier_f/dev/gbf-dev-01. All gates passed, and gates.json came out byte-identical (sha256 406e6413...): 10/10 solvability, 173 tokens, 4/4 variants reach V5, 12/12 mutants valid, kill rate 1.0. I ran every mutant myself, and each fails a check for its own 'breaks' property: frequency and sample-rate mutants fail peak_freq and band_fraction; the gain mutants and the bypass/rewire mutants fail max_abs and rms; the offset mutant fails mean (DC 0.126 after the gain), max_abs and band_fraction; square and triangle fail mean and band_fraction. Split discipline: signature_split(analog_sig_source_x|blocks_multiply_const_vxx|blocks_file_sink) = dev, and no test task uses that signature or any of the numbers 44.1 kHz, 2.8 kHz, 0.15 or 16 dB. The licence, source, cluster_id, provenance, review, perturbation (false, composed), family, level (L1, 3 functional blocks) and id/dir/split fields are all compliant. The canary appears only in task.json, and the instruction does not mention benchmarks or oracles. I rebuilt build.py twice in a scratch copy (~/grc-bench-work/review/gbf-dev-01/build_a and build_b); both builds are byte-identical to the committed task.json, reference.grc and all four variants. Tolerances follow the stated spec (±5 % amplitude, 1 % frequency, DC 0.01). Over-engineered correct answers still pass: band-pass filters (transition widths 100-500 Hz), a 3.5 kHz low-pass, a DC blocker, and gain 6.31 or 6.0. Answers that should fail do fail: a Head below 8192 samples, and gain errors of 1 dB or more. The contamination report shows no flags for this item. Minor non-blocking notes: (a) the build.py comment gives RMS 0.669238, but the true value is 0.669231 (task.json is correct). (b) The bypass and rewire_input mutants behave identically, so there are 11 distinct mutants rather than 12, still well over 5. (c) The disjointness line is accurate, but the closest training spec is GRC-Agent scenario 25: a float 1 kHz tone through a linear x3 Embedded-Python gain into a Null Sink. The difference rests on the dB specification, the numbers and the file output; it might be worth naming that explicitly. Scratch scripts are in the session scratchpad under rev_dev01/. I did not edit any task file; the only write to the task dir was the gates run, which left gates.json byte-identical.

findings.claim: The 'single clean tone' check (band_fraction 2700-2900 Hz, min 0.99) measures leakage from an unwindowed 8192-point FFT rather than the stated requirement. Some pure single tones that the frequency check accepts (±28 Hz) fail it, even though all of their power is within 100 Hz of 2.8 kHz. The reference passes only because 2800 Hz happens to sit 0.09 bins from a bin centre.
findings.evidence: Ladder run of the reference with freq=2786 (a pure cosine, gain 10**(16/20)): peak_freq 2788.55 passes, max_abs 0.946436 passes, rms 0.669246 passes, mean passes, band_fraction 0.988976 FAILS, so V5 fails. Offline with oracles.band_fraction (N=8192, fs=44100): 47 of 225 pure-tone frequencies in 2772-2828 Hz (0.25 Hz steps) fall below 0.99 (worst 0.9883 at 2823.5 Hz). At exactly 2800 Hz the value is 0.99835, so leakage alone uses about 17 % of the 1 % budget. In practice a faithful answer is at exactly 2800 Hz and passes. This is an inconsistency between the two tolerances, not a failure seen on any plausible answer: 4 variants and 5 over-engineered filtered/DC-blocked answers I tried all pass.
findings.suggested_fix: Make the purity check consistent with the frequency tolerance. Either widen the band to 2650-2950 Hz and say 'within 150 Hz of 2.8 kHz' in the instruction (min 0.9924 over the whole ±28 Hz range, 0 failures), or lower min to 0.98 and say 'at least 98 %' (0 failures). Square (0.264), triangle (0.141) and DC-offset (0.932) mutants stay killed either way. The longer-term fix is a windowed band_fraction in oracles.py, which is shared code outside this task.

findings.claim: The instruction requires 'The flowgraph should keep running until it is stopped; do not limit the number of samples', but nothing checks this beyond 8192 delivered items. An answer that caps the output passes.
findings.evidence: Candidate answer = reference plus blocks_head(num_items=100000) before the File Sink: V5 passes with all checks true (peak 2799.3, max_abs 0.946436, rms 0.669299, band_fraction 0.99835). Only a cap below 8192 is rejected (head 4096 fails V4 liveness with 4096 items). _worker._run records finished_on_its_own, but neither V4 nor the oracle uses it. spec_properties already admits 'at least 8192 items delivered', so the instruction states more than is graded.
findings.suggested_fix: Either drop the 'do not limit the number of samples' clause, or reword it to what is graded (for example 'must produce at least 8192 samples; do not add a Head block'). If an unbounded run is really meant to be part of the spec, add a check that fails when the flowgraph finishes on its own. That needs harness support, which is outside this task directory.

findings.claim: The instruction asks for 'a test-tone generator with a gain stage' ('amplify it by 16 dB'). Variant v1_amp_on_source has no gain stage (the gain is folded into the Signal Source amplitude) and is listed as a correct solution. spec_properties also says the amplitude checks reject 'a missing gain stage'. The item record contradicts itself on whether a separate gain stage is required.
findings.evidence: variants/v1_amp_on_source.grc holds only analog_sig_source_x (amp '0.15 * 10**(16/20)') feeding blocks_file_sink, and reaches V5 in gates.json. spec_properties[2] says the amplitude checks reject '... a missing gain stage'. Structure is not graded, so a reviewer who reads the instruction literally would call v1 non-compliant. The gates still pass without v1 (v2, v3 and v4 all have an explicit gain stage).
findings.suggested_fix: Make it explicit that only the output is graded, for example 'Generate ... and amplify it by 16 dB (how you apply the gain is up to you)'. Also reword spec_properties to 'rejects an output without the 16 dB gain' instead of 'a missing gain stage'. Alternatively, drop v1 and keep the three variants that use an explicit gain stage.
